subtitle: From Forest Ember to Crowned Flame

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a shadowed forest edge opening onto distant Pallava camps
panels.action: Mayurasharma stands at the edge of the dense Sriparvata forest, half in shadow and half in light, clutching a spear as distant Pallava war tents and watchfires glow on the plain below.

dialogue.text: Hunted in Kanchi, hidden in Sriparvata, Mayurasharma now wages a forest war that forces the mighty Pallavas to crown his fury as a kingdom.

i18n.hi: कांची में शिकार, श्रीपर्वत में ओझल, अब मयूरशर्मा ऐसी जंगल-जंग छेड़ता है कि पराक्रमी पल्लव उसकी ज्वाला को ही राज्य का मुकुट बना देते हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in from high forest canopy down to hidden ravine
panels.action: Under the tall, dark canopy of Sriparvata, Mayurasharma sits on a rock in a narrow ravine, armor simple but eyes burning, as a few armed followers listen in tense silence.

dialogue.text: After the quarrel at Kanchi’s sacrifice halls, Mayurasharma vanished into the forests of Sriparvata, his wounded pride now shaping a new, harsher resolve.

i18n.hi: कांची के यज्ञशालाओं की तकरार के बाद मयूरशर्मा श्रीपर्वत के जंगलों में गुम हो गया, आहत अभिमान अब उसके भीतर नया, सख्त संकल्प घड़ रहा था।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Mayurasharma’s face lit by flickering firelight
panels.action: By a small forest fire, Mayurasharma leans forward, jaw set, tracing lines in the earth with a stick as a map of hills and roads takes shape beside his bare feet.

dialogue.text: The student who once came to Kanchi for sacred learning now drew paths of ambush and tribute in the dust, treating the forest as his fortress and school of war.

i18n.hi: जो छात्र कभी कांची ज्ञान के लिए आया था, अब धूल में घात और लगान की रेखाएं खींचता, जंगल को ही किला और युद्ध-गुरुकुल बना रहा था।

panels.shot: wide shot of forest track with a small armed band emerging from shadows
panels.action: Mayurasharma strides at the head of a lean band of warriors along a narrow forest track, their simple shields and spears catching faint dawn light as mist curls around them.

dialogue.text: Talagunda remembers him taking shelter in Sriparvata’s woods, gathering men who knew every ridge and ravine better than the polished marble of Kanchi’s courts.

i18n.hi: तालगुंडा बताता है, वह श्रीपर्वत के वन में डेरा डालता, ऐसे लोगों को जोड़ता जो हर पहाड़ी-घाटी को कांची की संगमरमर अदालतों से बेहतर जानते थे।

panels.shot: nighttime bird’s-eye shot over a small frontier village near forest edge
panels.action: Under a moonlit sky, a modest village at the forest’s edge lies still as Mayurasharma’s men stand at its outskirts, their torches unlit, while a few village elders approach in wary submission.

dialogue.text: From this shelter he began to levy tribute on nearby rulers and chiefs, not with royal seals, but with sudden arrivals at night and quiet demands at dawn.

i18n.hi: यहीं से वह पास के राजाओं-नायकों से लगान लेने लगा, मुहरों से नहीं, रात के धावे और भोर की खामोश मांगों से।

panels.shot: medium shot at ground level of Mayurasharma and a trembling chieftain
panels.action: At the village boundary, Mayurasharma stands calm and stern before a trembling local chieftain who offers a small chest of coins and grain, forest hills looming behind them.

dialogue.speaker: mayurasharma
dialogue.text: Your dues will no longer go only to Kanchi. The forest also has a lord.

i18n.hi: अब तुम्हारा कर सिर्फ कांची नहीं लेगी। जंगल का भी एक स्वामी है।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of a Pallava border camp in disarray
panels.action: A Pallava frontier camp lies in agitated disarray at first light, soldiers scrambling among toppled supplies and overturned carts while Mayurasharma’s band slips back toward the tree line in the distance.

dialogue.text: Talagunda says he troubled Pallava camps from his forest base, appearing as a sudden storm at their frontier tents and vanishing before the full army could turn.

i18n.hi: तालगुंडा कहता है, वह वन-दुर्ग से पल्लव छावनियों को सताता, सीमा के तंबुओं पर तूफान-सा टूटता और पूरी सेना संभलने से पहले गायब हो जाता।

panels.shot: low-angle shot from inside a Pallava tent flap, looking out
panels.action: From within a grand Pallava tent, the scene frames Mayurasharma at a distance leading his men away down a dusty track, a fallen Pallava banner left behind near disturbed supplies.

dialogue.text: These were not set battles of the field, but cuts and slashes at the edges of empire, each raid a question thrown at Pallava pride.

i18n.hi: ये खुले मैदान की साफ़ जंग नहीं थीं, बल्कि साम्राज्य की हदों पर चीरे और वार थे, हर धावा पल्लव अभिमान पर उठा एक सवाल।

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot showing multiple frontier landscapes
panels.action: In a composite scene spanning the frame, Mayurasharma’s standard appears before a rocky hill fortress, a scrubland outpost, and a riverside settlement, evoking different chiefs and polities like faint silhouettes in the background.

dialogue.text: Later, at Chandravalli, his scribes would recite a longer list—Traikutas, Abhiras, Sendrakas, Punnatas and others—names of neighbors claimed as cowed or confronted by this forest-born power.

i18n.hi: बाद में चंद्रवल्ली में उसके लेखक लंबी गिनती सुनाते—त्रिकूट, आभीर, सेन्द्रक, पुन्नट और कई और—पड़ोसियों के वे नाम जिन्हें यह वनजन्मी शक्ति झुका या ललकार चुकी थी।

panels.shot: tight focus on an inscription being chiseled into rock
panels.action: A sculptor chisels carefully into a rock face, the grooves of early Kadamba letters emerging as a court scribe oversees, while a younger Mayurasharma watches, arms folded, in the background.

dialogue.text: The Chandravalli record speaks with the pride of victory, yet the historian must hear in its bold lines both memory and exaggeration, both fact and crafted boast.

i18n.hi: चंद्रवल्ली का लेख विजय की ठसक से बोलता है, पर इतिहासकार को उसमें एक साथ स्मृति और अतिशयोक्ति, तथ्य और गढ़ी हुई शान दोनों सुनाई देते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot in a forest clearing with messengers arriving
panels.action: In a forest clearing that now feels like an open court, Mayurasharma sits on a simple wooden seat as messengers arrive from different directions, each bearing distinct gifts—cloth, coins, and baskets of produce.

dialogue.text: What began as a fugitive’s camp slowly hardened into a state’s first skeleton: streams of tribute, oaths of protection, and the quiet understanding that rule had changed hands.

i18n.hi: जो बस एक भगोड़े का डेरा था, धीरे-धीरे राज्य की पहली हड्डियों में बदल गया: लगान की धाराएं, रक्षा की शपथें, और यह शांत समझ कि राज बदल चुका है।

panels.shot: sweeping wide shot of a Pallava council hall
panels.action: Inside a stately Pallava hall, nobles and officers sit in a semicircle, faces tense, as a commander gestures toward a map where the region of Sriparvata and Banavasi is marked with a different emblem.

dialogue.text: For the Pallavas, each report from Sriparvata was a thorn: a former student, now a rebel lord, refusing to be only a name in their list of punished offenders.

i18n.hi: पल्लवों के लिए श्रीपर्वत से आती हर खबर कांटा थी: पुराना शिष्य, अब बागी नायक, जो उनकी दंडितों की सूची में बस एक नाम बनने से इनकार कर रहा था।

panels.shot: medium two-shot of a Pallava envoy and Mayurasharma
panels.action: On neutral ground near the forest edge, a richly robed Pallava envoy stands facing Mayurasharma, who wears simpler but now regal garments, both men steady and formal as their attendants watch closely.

dialogue.text: Talagunda speaks of an end to this long harassment: the Pallava lords, faced with a stubborn fire they could not stamp out, accepted Mayurasharma as their friend and sovereign in his sphere.

i18n.hi: तालगुंडा इस दीर्घ सताने के अंत की भी बात करता है: पल्लव नायक, उस द stubborn आग को न बुझा पाने पर, मयूरशर्मा को उसके क्षेत्र में मित्र और स्वामी मान लेते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on hands exchanging a symbolic object
panels.action: In the center of the frame, the Pallava envoy’s hand extends a finely worked ceremonial ring while Mayurasharma’s hand receives it firmly, forest hills faintly visible beyond their joined hands.

dialogue.speaker: mayurasharma
dialogue.text: Let it be known: the forest is no rebel’s den, but a kingdom.

i18n.hi: घोषणा हो: यह जंगल अब गद्दारों का अड्डा नहीं, एक राज्य है।

panels.shot: grand wide shot of Banavasi landscape with early town structures
panels.action: The view opens over Banavasi’s lush river plain, where new timber halls, granaries, and small shrines rise amid older huts, as Mayurasharma rides along a track, inspecting the growing town.

dialogue.text: With recognition came the work of order: Banavasi, once another forest-side settlement, became the beating heart of the Kadamba realm, binding tribute, justice and worship into one frame.

i18n.hi: मान्यता के साथ व्यवस्था का काम आया: बनवासी, जो कभी एक और वन-किनारे का बसाव था, कदंब राज्य की धड़कन बना, जहां लगान, न्याय और पूजा एक ढांचे में बंधे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Mayurasharma presiding over a land grant ceremony
panels.action: In an open courtyard, Mayurasharma sits on a low throne as brahmans stand before him, hands joined, while officials unroll a copper plate grant, an altar fire burning steadily to one side.

dialogue.text: Kadamba records remember him as both warrior and patron, granting brahmadeya lands and using the tools of the very order that once humiliated him to now legitimize his own throne.

i18n.hi: कदंब लेख उसे योद्धा भी याद रखते हैं, दाता भी—जो ब्रह्मदेय भूमि देता है और उसी व्यवस्था के औजारों से अपना सिंहासन वैध करता है जिसने कभी उसे अपमानित किया था।

panels.shot: symbolic shot of a white horse near a sacrificial post (no violence)
panels.action: A splendid white horse, richly adorned, is tethered calmly near a decorated post, priests and officials gathered respectfully at a distance, with Mayurasharma standing composed, hands folded across his chest.

dialogue.text: Later Halasi plates claim that he performed ashvamedha rites, embracing the highest symbols of sovereignty, declaring that a once-insulted student now strode the ritual path of emperors.

i18n.hi: बाद की हलसी ताम्रपट कहते हैं कि उसने अश्वमेध किए, सार्वभौम सत्ता के सर्वोच्च चिह्न अपनाए, यह जता कर कि कभी अपमानित शिष्य अब सम्राटों की यज्ञ-परंपरा पर चल रहा है।

panels.shot: intimate close-up of Mayurasharma looking at an inscription pillar
panels.action: At Talagunda, an older Mayurasharma stands with head slightly bowed before a freshly erected pillar, its inscription gleaming in the sun, his reflection faint in the polished stone.

dialogue.text: Yet the same pillar that praises his raids and taxes also speaks of a man who turned fury into structure, making the forest not just a refuge, but the root of a dynasty.

i18n.hi: पर वही स्तंभ, जो उसके धावे और कर की शान गाता है, यह भी बताता है एक ऐसे आदमी का, जिसने क्रोध को ढांचे में बदला, जंगल को केवल शरण नहीं, एक वंश की जड़ बना दिया।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot blending forest, town, and distant Pallava land
panels.action: The scene blends Sriparvata’s dark forests in the foreground, the rising townscape of Banavasi in the middle, and far on the horizon the faint silhouette of Kanchi’s temples under a hazy sky, as Mayurasharma stands between forest and city.

dialogue.text: His story reminds us that rebellion becomes statecraft not when swords strike hardest, but when a restless fire learns to govern, to tax, to grant, and to stand as an equal among powers.

i18n.hi: उसकी कथा याद दिलाती है: विद्रोह राज्यकला तब बनता है, जब तलवार की चोट से आगे, बेचैन ज्वाला राज सीखती है—कर लगाना, दान देना, शासन करना, और शक्तियों के बीच समकक्ष खड़ा होना।

subtitle_i18n.en: From Forest Ember to Crowned Flame
